title: Customers Who Never Order
description:
Table `Customers` holds all customers and table `Orders` holds orders placed, referencing `Customers.id` via `customerId`.

Write a query to report the names of all customers who have **never** placed an order. Name the output column `Customers`.

Return the result in any order.
solutionSql:
SELECT c.name AS Customers
FROM Customers c
LEFT JOIN Orders o ON c.id = o.customerId
WHERE o.id IS NULL;
hint: An anti-join (LEFT JOIN ... WHERE right side IS NULL) or NOT EXISTS both work. Watch out: NOT IN returns nothing at all if the subquery contains a NULL.
outputExplanation: Henry and Max have no orders and are the two customers reported. Joe and Sam both have at least one order and are excluded.

tests.name: Example
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Customers VALUES (1,'Joe'),(2,'Henry'),(3,'Sam'),(4,'Max');
INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,3),(2,1);

INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,1),(2,2);

tests.name: Single customer, has ordered
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,1);

tests.name: NULL customerId — NOT IN returns empty
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Customers VALUES (1,'Joe'),(2,'Henry'),(3,'Sam');
INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,1),(2,NULL);

tests.name: All orders have NULL customerId
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Customers VALUES (1,'Joe'),(2,'Henry');
INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,NULL),(2,NULL);

tests.name: Two customers share a name, one has ordered
tests.seedSql:
INSERT INTO Customers VALUES (1,'Alex'),(2,'Alex'),(3,'Ravi');
INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,3);

tests.name: Customer with NULL name, no orders
Orphan order plus a valid order
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,99),(2,1);

tests.name: One customer with many orders, the other never ordered
tests.seedSql:

INSERT INTO Orders VALUES (1,1),(2,1),(3,1),(4,1);

tests.name: All customers ordered except one
tests.seedSql:

tests.name: All orders reference non-existent customers
tests.seedSql:
